clue.text: Great day! Old boy needs raincoat going up country

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the string is read from bottom to top, so backwards

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, written with the letter I standing in for the 1
D is the standard abbreviation for day
OB is the usual abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a mac (mackintosh) is a raincoat

explanation.surface: An excited cry about a great day, followed by an old boy putting on his raincoat as he heads north into the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great day!' reads as an exclamation, but it splits into two separate pieces; everything from Great to raincoat is then read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambodia is a nation in South-East Asia, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Group around bar suffering reversal in game

indicators.note: around says the first word's letters wrap about the next word's letters
suffering a reversal means the whole combination is then turned back to front

blocks.note: a set is a group of things that belong together
an inn is a pub, a bar

explanation.surface: A band of players gathered round a bar suffer a setback during a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport, so it is an example of a game.

clue.text: After a terrible start score with some difficulty

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so these letters are knocked out of their order

blocks.note: taken as written
the word start, rearranged
to score a surface is to scratch or etch it

explanation.surface: Someone who began badly then struggled to get any points on the board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the jumbled start after the A, and score is a verb here, not points.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at a stretch means only just managing it, at the limit of what is possible.

clue.text: Soldier in Cornish resort's something smuggled in swimwear?

indicators.note: in says the soldier is placed inside the resort's name

blocks.note: GI is an American private soldier
Bude is a seaside town in Cornwall, England

explanation.surface: A soldier in a Cornish seaside town apparently hiding contraband in his trunks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Budgie smugglers' is Australian and British slang for tight men's swimming briefs, hence the playful question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A budgie (budgerigar, a small parakeet) is what the slang term for skimpy trunks jokingly claims is being smuggled.

clue.text: Collection of 11 on to be cooked with butcher paid — scandalous fact?

indicators.note: food that is cooked is transformed, so these letters are to be mixed up

blocks.note: 11 across is a word for what dogs chew; a full set of them makes up a body's framework
taken as written, as part of the letters to rearrange
taken as written, the rest of the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Bones to be cooked once the butcher is paid sounds like a shady kitchen secret.
explanation.walkthrough: The 11 refers to 11 across; 'with' joins on to butcher paid so that all thirteen letters are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A skeleton in the cupboard is an idiom for a shameful secret that someone keeps hidden.

clue.text: Feeble type with mischievous child

blocks.note: W is a common abbreviation for with
an imp is a naughty child

explanation.surface: A weak person saddled with a naughty youngster.
explanation.definitionFit: A wimp is a timid, weak person, so a synonym for a feeble type.

clue.text: Put pins round seat covering tailor's frame

indicators.note: covering means the seat word goes over and around the other letters
a frame is the outer edge, so only the end letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: a saddle is the seat on a horse or bicycle
the first and last letters of tailor

explanation.surface: A tailor fitting a seat cover by putting pins round its frame.
explanation.walkthrough: Pins is slang for legs, so putting your legs round something is sitting astride it.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle is to sit or stand with legs either side of something, so pins (legs) are put around it.

clue.text: Idolise at all during Religious Education?

indicators.note: during places the phrase within the other piece, as an event happens within a period

blocks.note: RE is the school subject Religious Education
ever means at all, as in 'if ever'

explanation.surface: Asking whether a pupil idolises anyone at all during a religious studies lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere someone is to worship or deeply respect them, a synonym of idolise.

clue.text: Stunned in struggle for possession, led by a point

blocks.note: taken as written
west is a point of the compass
in rugby a ruck is a scrum-like contest for the loose ball

explanation.surface: A player left dazed in a fight for the ball, with a single point separating the sides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Led by' puts A and the compass point in front of the struggle; point is a direction, not a score.
explanation.definitionFit: Awestruck means overwhelmed with wonder, so dumbfounded or stunned.

clue.text: See 5
Dog treats 22 across 26?

blocks.note: first meaning: what dogs are given to gnaw
second meaning: the nickname of the Star Trek doctor at 22/26

explanation.walkthrough: 22 across 26 is the Star Trek medic Leonard McCoy, whom Captain Kirk calls by a nickname from 'sawbones', slang for a surgeon.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogs chew bones as treats, and Bones is the Starship Enterprise doctor's nickname.

clue.text: Film of some value that's all over the Oscars?

definitions.text: Film of some value that's all over the Oscars?

blocks.note: surface reading: a movie worth something, perhaps a winner
setter's reading: a thin precious-metal coating that covers the Academy Award statuettes

explanation.walkthrough: Film suggests cinema, helped by the Oscars, but it means a thin layer; the statuettes are metal coated in a precious yellow finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold plate is a thin coating of the precious metal, and Oscar statuettes are finished with one.

clue.text: News boss about to join army shows merit

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the boss's title is read backwards

blocks.note: ED is short for editor, the head of a newspaper
to serve is to be a member of the armed forces

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor about to enlist proves their worth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like 'on the point of', but about is the reversal signal and 'to' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: To deserve something is to have earned it, a synonym of the verb merit.

clue.text: Tyre so bald, sons twice pulled out foot-lever

indicators.note: pulled out means the named letters are removed from the word

blocks.note: a bald tyre has no grip pattern left on it
S is the abbreviation for son, taken twice

explanation.surface: A tyre worn so smooth that two sons have to drag it off the car.
explanation.walkthrough: The first three words describe a word rather than giving one directly: a worn-out tyre is without tread.
explanation.definitionFit: A treadle is a pedal worked by the foot to drive a machine such as a sewing machine or loom.

clue.text: Blokes inside Ptolemy disturbed, creating work

indicators.note: disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the name's letters are rearranged
inside says the blokes are placed within the other letters

blocks.note: the name Ptolemy, rearranged
blokes is British slang for men

explanation.surface: Men barging in on the ancient astronomer Ptolemy and upsetting his labours.
explanation.definitionFit: Employment is paid occupation, a synonym of work.

clue.text: Adoptee supposedly lucky to miss first course

indicators.note: to miss the first means the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: a mascot is a creature or figure adopted by a team because it is thought to bring luck

explanation.surface: An adopted child, thought to be fortunate, is about to skip the first course of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Course looks like part of a meal, but it is a racecourse; Ascot is a famous racecourse in Berkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a racecourse where the Royal Ascot meeting is held, so a course for horse racing.

clue.text: See 5
Wrong end of torpedo going off

indicators.note: the end of the word, going off, means its final letter is dropped
going off means departing, so that part leaves the word

blocks.note: to torpedo a ship is to sink it

explanation.surface: Something has gone wrong with the tail of a torpedo as it fires.
explanation.walkthrough: Torpedo is a verb here, not the weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A sin is a moral wrong, so the noun wrong is a synonym.

clue.text: Universal poacher initially going in wears bears out

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of the word is used
going in says the preceding letters enter the next word

blocks.note: U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal
the first letter of poacher
to sport something is to wear it, like a hat or a moustache

explanation.surface: A poacher who sneaks in wearing bearskins, or carrying bears out.
explanation.definitionFit: To support a claim is to bear it out, confirming it with evidence.

clue.text: Fold left trapped by decaying vegetable matter

indicators.note: trapped by means held inside the following word

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for left
peat is partly decayed plant material found in bogs

explanation.surface: Something left stuck in rotting compost, like a sheep left in the fold.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleat is a fold pressed into cloth, so the noun fold is a synonym.

clue.text: Old rocker in sexy underwear — I'm thrilled!

blocks.note: a teddy is a one-piece item of women's lingerie
'Boy!' or 'oh boy!' is a cry of delight

explanation.surface: An ageing rock-and-roller delighted at being in risqué lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits who followed rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A Teddy boy was a 1950s rock-and-roll fan, so now a rocker from long ago.

clue.text: Nick quiet: quiet sitting in cage

indicators.note: sitting in means placed inside the cage word

blocks.note: a coop is a cage for poultry
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: Someone told to keep quiet, very quiet, while locked in a cage.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick is British slang for a police station (and for arrest or steal); cop shop is the same in slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A cop shop is slang for a police station, which in British slang is also the nick.

clue.text: Small seal called out for young creature in river

indicators.note: called out means spoken, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: a signet is a small seal, often set in a ring

explanation.surface: A small seal barks to summon a youngster swimming in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Seal looks like the animal, which fits a river scene, but it is a stamp for wax.
explanation.definitionFit: A cygnet is a young swan, a creature found on rivers.

clue.text: Extremely dull romance developed with shy doctor

indicators.note: extremely means at the extremes, so only the end letters are taken
developed means grown into a new form, so these letters are reorganised

blocks.note: the first and last letters of dull
taken as written
coy means bashful, shy

explanation.surface: A very boring love affair turned serious with a bashful medic.
explanation.walkthrough: Leonard McCoy is the ship's doctor in the original Star Trek, played by DeForest Kelley.
explanation.definitionFit: Dr Leonard McCoy is the chief medical officer of the starship Enterprise, a fictional physician.

clue.text: Radiance of religious figure drawn into temptation

indicators.note: drawn into means pulled inside the following word

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
a lure is an enticement or temptation

explanation.surface: The glow of a holy figure who is drawn into sin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is a soft shine or glow, a synonym of radiance.

clue.text: Freezing cold in lorry

indicators.note: in says the letter is placed inside the vehicle's name

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
artic is British slang for an articulated lorry, a large truck

explanation.surface: A shivering driver complains it is freezing cold inside the truck cab.
explanation.walkthrough: Lorry is British for truck; an artic is the long kind with a hinged trailer.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctic is used informally of weather to mean bitterly cold, a synonym of freezing.

clue.text: Butcher's dividing merchandise, fetching property

indicators.note: dividing means splitting the next word apart by sitting in its middle

blocks.note: goods are items for sale
butcher's is Cockney rhyming slang: butcher's hook rhymes with look

explanation.surface: A butcher's shop cutting up its stock and putting an attractive property on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butcher's' looks like a shop, but it is rhyming slang ('have a butcher's'); fetching means attractive, not bringing.
explanation.definitionFit: Good looks are an attractive appearance, a quality that makes someone fetching.

clue.text: Escapee at Sodom hard and reluctant

blocks.note: in Genesis, Lot fled Sodom before its destruction
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Lot fleeing Sodom was tough, but unwilling to look back.
explanation.definitionFit: Loth (also loath) means unwilling, a synonym of reluctant.

clue.text: See 22
Show remorse having sent off one right winger

indicators.note: sent off means dismissed from the field, so a letter is removed

blocks.note: to regret is to show remorse
R is the abbreviation for right; only one of the two is removed

explanation.surface: A footballer is sorry after a right winger has been sent off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right winger' looks like a footballer or a politician; winger alone means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An egret is a heron-like bird, and a creature with wings is a winger in crossword terms.

clue.text: US shooter Jack disrupted nation

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown out of order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: jack and tar are both old words for a sailor
the word nation, rearranged

explanation.surface: An American gunman named Jack throws the country into chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: Shooter suggests a gunman, but it means someone who shoots films.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino is an American film director, and directors shoot films.
